From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd | AUD 24,000,000 | debt-free/cash-free | NSW law
**Status of Seller material:** Counterparty draft. Every characterisation below has been tested against the Seller's own Disclosure Letter and the DD references, and none has been accepted at face value.

## Headline: the cover note contradicts the Disclosure Letter

| Cover note says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|
| Bluefen consent "is addressed" | No final written consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied (DL 2) |
| Riverlark released "following Completion" | Facility not repaid and no discharge in the data room (DL 3), while a change-control clause (8.1) is triggered by the sale |
| DD-006 incident "not expected to be material" | Access, scope and notification obligation all unknown; investigation preliminary (DL 6) |
| Sandbar renewals are "ordinary course" | The DL expressly does not say whether they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued (DL 8) |
| Bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" | AUD 420k is not in the funds flow, and on-costs are unaddressed (DL 5). The Company is the employer, so the cost falls on the Buyer after Completion |

These contradictions should be put to Seller counsel in writing. The Disclosure Letter, not the cover note, is the document that limits our claims.

## Issue-by-issue

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 30–50% (AUD 7.2m–12m) if there is no W&I policy. 20% is acceptable only if W&I is in place and the cap clearly excludes fundamental, tax, specific indemnity, leakage and fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 40%. Be prepared to settle at 25–30% (or 20% plus W&I), with express carve-outs.
- **Reason:** Customer concentration (Bluefen ~30% of revenue), an open IP chain and a live privacy incident make the risk profile too high for a 20% general cap.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25k (~0.10%). Basket AUD 250k (~1.04%), deductible so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 10–15k, with related or similar claims aggregated. Basket at 0.5% (AUD 120k) on a **tipping** basis, so the first dollar is recoverable once the basket is reached. Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Accept a de minimis of about AUD 20k only with an aggregation clause. Insist on a tipping basket, at AUD 150k at most.
- **Reason:** A 1% deductible basket permanently absorbs AUD 250k of genuine loss, and without aggregation the de minimis can be used to split related claims below the threshold.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion for general warranties. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months, or at minimum one full audited financial year plus 3 months. Separate, longer periods for title, tax and indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months. Reject the "applies to all Claims" default (see N-014).
- **Reason:** 18 months may not cover a full post-Completion audit cycle, and the default wording would cut down every other claim category without anyone noticing.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Cap of 100% of the price (including any adjustments). No de minimis or basket. Not qualified by disclosure or knowledge. Claim period of at least 6 years, matching the NSW contract limitation period, or 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. This is non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, and a 20% cap would leave it AUD 19.2m short.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature", with no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that no limitation, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance or disclosure provision applies to any claim arising from fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct of the Seller or its officers, employees or advisers. It should also preserve claims that cannot be excluded at law, such as misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out and narrow the non-reliance clause.
- **Reason:** Fraud is unlikely to be excludable in any case, but silence invites argument, and the non-reliance clause could be used as an evidential shield against misrepresentation claims.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosures only, made against identified warranties. Each must meet a "fairly disclosed" standard, meaning enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect of the matter. At most, allow a narrow list of named searches made on a fixed date. Disclosure should not qualify fundamental or tax warranties or any indemnity. DL 1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable only if it does not dilute the standard.
- **Recommendation:** Strike DL 1.1 and most of DL 1.2. Accept DL 2–10 as specific disclosures, subject to the indemnities and CPs below.
- **Reason:** General data room disclosure moves the whole diligence risk onto the Buyer and empties the warranties of value.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** An express pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not reduce any claim. The fallback is to limit exclusion to matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Under no circumstances accept a "discoverable" or constructive-knowledge standard, or one that extends to advisers.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the clause excludes claims for every known issue in this deal (Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006), precisely where the Buyer most needs protection.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The CP is treated as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent".
- **Buyer wants:** A Completion CP requiring Bluefen's written consent under cl 11.2, in a form approved by the Buyer. It must be unconditional, or subject only to conditions acceptable to the Buyer. Evidence is required that every cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied. The CP should be waivable only by the Buyer, backed by an obligation on the Seller to use all reasonable endeavours, with a long-stop date and a Buyer walk right. A material adverse change in the Bluefen relationship should be a termination trigger.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller formulation and make this a hard CP.
- **Reason:** About AUD 3.6m (~30%) of revenue is at risk. "Any written consent" could be a conditional or onerous consent that Bluefen can later rely on.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** Release to be provided after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price through the funds flow. A payoff letter is needed before Completion, and an executed deed of release and PPSR/security discharges must be delivered at Completion. The ~AUD 3.2m (plus break costs, interest and fees) should be treated as Debt in the price mechanics. A PPSR search should also confirm there is no security over the sale shares.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. Make payoff and release a Completion deliverable.
- **Reason:** The sale triggers the change-control clause (cl 8.1), so the Company would be in default under a secured facility on Day 1, with no release in hand.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420k bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses, plus employer superannuation, payroll tax (NSW), workers' compensation and other on-costs, treated as Transaction Costs/Debt and deducted from the price. Alternatively, they should be paid by the Seller through Company payroll at Completion. A specific indemnity, outside caps and thresholds, should cover any shortfall and all related tax.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow as a price deduction, including on-costs.
- **Reason:** The Company is the employer and will bear the AUD 420k plus roughly 15–20% in on-costs, so "a matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the funds flow reflects it. Confirm current rates with payroll.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **CP:** Evidence of cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, verified by bank or Ironquay confirmation, and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - **Fallback:** A full indemnity, outside caps, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge, covering all Loss arising from any failure of title to SOW3 Project Materials. This includes third-party claims, injunctions, re-development or licensing costs and business interruption. It should have a claim period of at least 6 years and be supported by a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the payment-only indemnity.
- **Reason:** Under cl 7.3, title does not pass until payment clears, so the exposure is loss of core IP, not AUD 180k.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:** Complete the investigation, obtain an independent forensic report, and document the Notifiable Data Breaches assessment and any OAIC or individual notifications. The Buyer should have consultation and approval rights.
  - **Specific indemnity:** Outside the general cap, or under a separate high cap, and not qualified by disclosure or knowledge. It should cover regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, third-party and class claims, and customer claims (including from Bluefen).
  - **Security and warranties:** A retention or escrow, and an updated privacy compliance warranty brought down at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the Seller's characterisation, and require a specific indemnity plus a retention.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 personal records may be exposed with unknown access. The Privacy Act requires a suspected eligible breach to be assessed within 30 days, and we are now more than 6 weeks past the 22 September position, so a compliance failure may already exist.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Information:** Full information, including whether Sandbar is related to the Seller and why the commitment was split into three, which may have been done to avoid an approval threshold.
  - **Terms:** Confirmation of term, termination rights and accrual status.
  - **Protection:** Warranties that the renewals are arm's-length and in the ordinary course.
  - **Classification:** If the renewals are related-party, treat them as Leakage. If they are non-essential or non-terminable, cover them by a price adjustment or specific indemnity.
  - **Going forward:** Conduct-of-business covenants requiring Buyer consent for new commitments above a low threshold before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept until diligence closes. Reserve a price adjustment or indemnity.
- **Reason:** The DL itself declines to call these ordinary course, and splitting the commitment into three is a red flag.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise. Fundamental, tax and IP claims are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, express regimes for each category:
  - general warranties
  - fundamental (title and capacity) warranties
  - tax warranties and tax indemnity
  - each specific indemnity (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar if needed)
  - Leakage and price adjustment
  - covenants and Completion obligations
  - fraud

  Each should have its own cap, thresholds and time limit, and the default should be reversed: general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the default and redraft cl 12 as a matrix.
- **Reason:** The default is the mechanism that silently caps every other protection in this list.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Independent checks:** An ASIC company search and historical extract, a reconciliation of the register against ASIC, share certificates, and the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emption rights, options, convertibles).
  - **Searches:** PPSR searches against the Seller and Company, given the Riverlark security.
  - **Warranties and deliverables:** A fundamental title warranty that the shares are fully paid and free of Encumbrances and that no other securities or rights exist. Completion deliverables should include releases of any share security.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. Run the searches and back them with the fundamental warranty (see N-004).
- **Reason:** DL 10 itself concedes that the register is only the Seller's source, not a verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** These are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on bonuses and any consolidation exit issues. Full tax warranties, conduct-of-claims provisions, a period of at least the amendment period plus 3 months (target 5–7 years), and a cap of 100% of the price.
  - **IP:** Robust IP ownership, non-infringement and open-source warranties, elevated in cap and duration given Ironquay.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as **open**, not settled, and table full tax and IP drafting.
- **Reason:** Placing tax and IP inside a 20%/18-month regime is a substantive concession, not an administrative point.

## Also noted (not in the list)
- **Lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9):** The DL says these are notification and assignment restrictions only. Confirm on the source documents whether change of control triggers any consent or termination right, and add a warranty that no material contract has a change-of-control right other than as specifically disclosed.
- **W&I:** If W&I insurance is pursued, the policy exclusions will almost certainly cover the known matters (Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses), so specific indemnities are still required.

## Priority for the mark-up
1. **Walk-away or hard CP items:** N-004, N-005, N-008, N-009, N-014.
2. **Price-protecting items:** N-010, N-011, N-012, N-013.
3. **Negotiable on quantum:** N-001, N-002, N-003.

I recommend a cover reply that records the contradictions in the headline table and states that the Buyer does not accept the cover note's characterisations.

- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses, plus employer superannuation, payroll tax (NSW), workers' compensation and other on-costs, treated as Transaction Costs/Debt and deducted from the price. Alternatively, they should be paid by the Seller through Company payroll at Completion. A specific indemnity, outside caps and thresholds, should cover any shortfall and all related tax.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow as a price deduction, including on-costs.
- **Reason:** The Company is the employer and will bear the AUD 420k plus roughly 15–20% in on-costs, so "a matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the funds flow reflects it. Confirm current rates with payroll.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **CP:** Evidence of cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, verified by bank or Ironquay confirmation, and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - **Fallback:** A full indemnity, outside caps, thresholds, disclosure and knowledge, covering all Loss arising from any failure of title to SOW3 Project Materials. This includes third-party claims, injunctions, re-development or licensing costs and business interruption. It should have a claim period of at least 6 years and be supported by a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the payment-only indemnity.
- **Reason:** Under cl 7.3, title does not pass until payment clears, so the exposure is loss of core IP, not AUD 180k.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:** Complete the investigation, obtain an independent forensic report, and document the Notifiable Data Breaches assessment and any OAIC or individual notifications. The Buyer should have consultation and approval rights.
  - **Specific indemnity:** Outside the general cap, or under a separate high cap, and not qualified by disclosure or knowledge. It should cover regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, third-party and class claims, and customer claims (including from Bluefen).
  - **Security and warranties:** A retention or escrow, and an updated privacy compliance warranty brought down at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the Seller's characterisation, and require a specific indemnity plus a retention.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 personal records may be exposed with unknown access. The Privacy Act requires a suspected eligible breach to be assessed within 30 days, and we are now more than 6 weeks past the 22 September position, so a compliance failure may already exist.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k in total) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Information:** Full information, including whether Sandbar is related to the Seller and why the commitment was split into three, which may have been done to avoid an approval threshold.
  - **Terms:** Confirmation of term, termination rights and accrual status.
  - **Protection:** Warranties that the renewals are arm's-length and in the ordinary course.
  - **Classification:** If the renewals are related-party, treat them as Leakage. If they are non-essential or non-terminable, cover them by a price adjustment or specific indemnity.
  - **Going forward:** Conduct-of-business covenants requiring Buyer consent for new commitments above a low threshold before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept until diligence closes. Reserve a price adjustment or indemnity.
- **Reason:** The DL itself declines to call these ordinary course, and splitting the commitment into three is a red flag.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise. Fundamental, tax and IP claims are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, express regimes for each category:
  - general warranties
  - fundamental (title and capacity) warranties
  - tax warranties and tax indemnity
  - each specific indemnity (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar if needed)
  - Leakage and price adjustment
  - covenants and Completion obligations
  - fraud

  Each should have its own cap, thresholds and time limit, and the default should be reversed: general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the default and redraft cl 12 as a matrix.
- **Reason:** The default is the mechanism that silently caps every other protection in this list.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Independent checks:** An ASIC company search and historical extract, a reconciliation of the register against ASIC, share certificates, and the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emption rights, options, convertibles).

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** These are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on bonuses and any consolidation exit issues. Full tax warranties, conduct-of-claims provisions, a period of at least the amendment period plus 3 months (target 5–7 years), and a cap of 100% of the price.
  - **IP:** Robust IP ownership, non-infringement and open-source warranties, elevated in cap and duration given Ironquay.
- **Recommendation:** Treat both as **open**, not settled, and table full tax and IP drafting.
- **Reason:** Placing tax and IP inside a 20%/18-month regime is a substantive concession, not an administrative point.
